      "text": "Why does the coinsdb read error test fail without IPC on 32-bit systems?",

      "other_replies": [
        "rc:2664068476"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:2679121949",
      "status_by_quote": "The trick was that on 64-bit systems, LevelDB uses mmap which reflects file changes immediately - this is what we we're "

      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "Add verification, such as asserting a debug log, that the read error callback is executed in the functional test.",

      "type": "suggestion",

      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author declined, preferring simple local try-catch and noting HaveCoin removal",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:2724446763"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:2724446763",
      "status_by_quote": "It's a simple try-catch, I don't see the point in extending the call stack even more, we don't do that in other cases an"

      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Keep an optimized existence check on the database backing view that avoids copying, caching, or deserialization.",

      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "safety",

    },

      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "approach",

      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "maintenance",
      "text": "The callback chain to the GUI message box before abort is convoluted and difficult to trace thread safety for across threads and locks.",
      "quote": "Tracing through callback logic safety (\"It must be safe to call from any thread, with or without locks held\") isn't very straightforward, so it would be nice to not have to do that.",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "open",
